# BotsDoThat

> There's a bot for that. Here's how. A live, sourced feed of real things people hand to AI agents (inbox and phone calls, shopping, travel, family, health, work, small business), with real popularity numbers, plain-English guides, copy-paste prompts, build-your-own-bot blueprints and tips to run your bots for less.

Data as of 2026-10-30. Popularity numbers are real counts (X likes/reposts, Reddit upvotes) with the date measured; unknown values are omitted.

## Start here
- [What is an AI agent? (in simple terms)](https://botsdothat.com/what-can-bots-do/): plain-English explainer, AI agent vs. chatbot, what agents can and can't do safely
- [How much does it cost to run an AI agent?](https://botsdothat.com/how-much-does-it-cost-to-run-an-ai-agent/): Monthly estimates for 11 everyday bots at official API prices, with the math shown.
- [OpenClaw vs Hermes Agent: a beginner's guide](https://botsdothat.com/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent/): What each open-source agent is, side-by-side comparison, how to pick, cost and safety tips.
- [Is it safe to give an AI agent your email and calendar?](https://botsdothat.com/is-it-safe-to-give-an-ai-agent-your-email/): Prompt injection, too much access, sending without review, and 8 rules that keep you in charge.
- [How to build an AI agent without coding](https://botsdothat.com/how-to-build-an-ai-agent-without-coding/): step-by-step beginner guide using a real blueprint as the worked example
- [AI agent examples for everyday life](https://botsdothat.com/ai-agent-examples/): every example on one page, grouped by part of life
- [Trending now](https://botsdothat.com/trending/)
- [Bot blueprints](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/): build-your-own-bot recipes
- [Latest in AI](https://botsdothat.com/news/): new models, agent launches and AI price changes in plain words, with sources (RSS: https://botsdothat.com/news/feed.xml)
- [Run your bots for less](https://botsdothat.com/run-your-bots-for-less/): how to reduce AI API costs (model choice, free tiers, caching, batch, schedules, spend limits)
- [AI agent cost calculator](https://botsdothat.com/run-your-bots-for-less/#calculator): pick a bot or enter runs and message size, compare monthly cost across 20 models from official prices checked 2026-10-27; prefill with ?bot=<blueprint-slug>
- [AI price table](https://botsdothat.com/ai-pricing/): official API and plan prices for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI, Groq, Mistral, Meta and DeepSeek, checked 2026-10-27
- [RSS feed of new use cases](https://botsdothat.com/feed.xml)

## Use cases by category

### Inbox, calls & paperwork
- [Have your bot catch calendar clashes hiding in your email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/catch-calendar-clashes-hiding-in-your-email/): Plans don't only live in your calendar. A rescheduled event in a confirmation email, or a "call Mom at 2" note you emailed yourself, can quietly clash with what's booked. An always-on agent can compare your email with your calendar every morning and text you before a clash, but in WIRED's test of six agents only two caught one on their own, so ask for this check by name.
- [Let ChatGPT catch you up on your iCloud Mail and update your iPhone calendar](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-chatgpt-run-your-icloud-mail-and-calendar/): If your email ends in @icloud.com, @me.com or @mac.com, ChatGPT can now read and search it, draft replies and add or move events on the calendar you see on your iPhone. It works on every ChatGPT plan, including Free, and ChatGPT's always-on dots can use it too.
- [Put together a home or car insurance claim with an AI agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/put-together-an-insurance-claim-with-an-ai-agent/): Drop your photos, receipts and policy into one folder and let an agent build the damage list, a dated timeline and the questions to ask your insurer. You check every line and file the claim yourself.
- [Let your bot sign in without seeing your passwords](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-bot-sign-in-without-seeing-your-passwords/): Agents get stuck at login pages, and pasting your password into a chat is risky. With 1Password for Agents, your bot asks to use a saved login, you approve it on your phone, and 1Password types it in, so the bot never sees the password.
- [Let a bot answer your phone and take messages for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-a-bot-answer-and-screen-your-calls/): Forward your calls to an agent with its own phone number. It picks up, says it's your AI assistant, talks to the caller, takes a message and sends you a short summary. People who use it say many spam callers simply hang up.
- [Send a long video or thread to your bot with one reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/send-a-long-video-or-thread-to-your-bot/): See a long video or X thread you don't have time for? Reply to it by tagging your bot, and a short summary waits for you in your bot's app later.
- [Send all your newsletters to your bot and get one daily report](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/newsletter-daily-report/): Subscribe your newsletters to your bot's own email address. It reads every issue and sends you one short report each day, with a score that tells you which ones are worth reading in full.
- [Have your bot make a customer-service phone call for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/make-a-customer-service-call/): Some jobs still need a phone call, like cancelling a service or sorting out an account. With a phone-calling add-on, your bot can make the call, sit on hold and report back.
- [Hand your most-hated weekly chores to a personal agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-your-most-hated-chores-to-a-personal-agent/): Personal agents like Meta Muse, Grok Bot and Gemini Spark work in the background on a schedule. Start with the chore you hate most.
- [Get a daily scam check on your inbox](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/email-scam-filter/): A read-only bot reads your new email each morning and gives each suspicious message a risk score and the red flags.
- [Have a bot sort your scanned paper mail and flag what needs you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sort-scanned-paper-mail-with-alerts/): A virtual mailbox service scans your paper mail to email. The bot reads every letter, queues up the routine ones for your OK, and pulls you in only when something looks unusual.
- [Give your agent its own email address](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/give-your-agent-its-own-email-address/): Give your agent an inbox of its own. Then you or anyone else can forward it jobs, like a meeting request it turns into a calendar invite with prep notes.
- [Get a Monday recap of your inbox and a to-do list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/monday-inbox-recap-and-todo/): Every Monday a bot reviews last week's email, recaps what matters and suggests a ranked to-do list.
- [Only see the emails that actually need a reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/flag-only-emails-that-need-a-reply/): A simple triage bot flags anything needing a reply within 24 hours and moves the noise out of the way.
- [Get a short morning digest on topics you care about](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/morning-news-digest/): A bot reads the news on your topics every morning and sends you a short plain-English digest, or even an audio version.
- [Watch your email for one important letter or reply](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-for-one-important-letter/): Waiting on a visa decision, a parcel or a reply from the landlord? Have a bot watch for it and ping you.
- [Understand a confusing letter or notice, and what to do next](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/understand-a-confusing-letter/): A letter from a government office, insurer, bank or landlord landed in your mailbox and you can't tell if it's important, a bill, a scam, or nothing.
- [Write a complaint that actually gets a problem fixed](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-complaint-that-gets-fixed/): A company messed up (late delivery, broken product, wrong charge, bad repair) and customer service keeps going in circles.
- [Get through a long form without the headache](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/fill-out-a-long-form/): A long application or government form is confusing, and you're not sure what each question is really asking.
- [Review a rental lease before you sign](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/review-a-lease-before-signing/): The lease is long, the landlord wants it signed this week, and you're worried about what's buried in it.
- [Make a moving checklist and change your address everywhere](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/moving-checklist-and-change-of-address/): Moving means telling dozens of companies and offices your new address, and something always gets missed.
- [Get your email inbox under control](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/clean-up-your-email-inbox/): Thousands of unread emails, and the important ones get buried under newsletters and promos.

### Run your bots for less
- [Set spend limits and usage alerts on your AI accounts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/set-ai-spend-limits-and-alerts/): Before a bot runs on autopilot, put a hard cap on what it can spend and check usage weekly, so a runaway loop can't run up a big bill.
- [Keep your bot's prompts, tools and context short](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-prompts-and-context-short/): You pay for everything the model reads on every run: your instructions, tool definitions, pasted pages and the conversation so far. Trimming those is often the easiest saving.
- [Stop always-on bots burning tokens: run them less often](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/schedule-bots-without-burning-tokens/): Every scheduled run costs tokens, even when nothing has changed. Match the schedule to how often the thing really changes, and switch fun-but-idle bots to run only when you ask.
- [Run open AI models on your own computer for simple jobs](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/run-open-models-on-your-own-computer/): Open-weight models can run on your own computer with a free tool like Ollama, so routine jobs cost nothing per message. Some hosts also run open models for a fraction of big-model prices.
- [Cut your AI bill with prompt caching and batch discounts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/cut-costs-with-caching-and-batch/): If your bot sends the same long instructions every time, caching makes the repeat part much cheaper. If results can wait a few hours, batch processing halves the price at several providers.
- [Decide between a monthly AI plan and paying per use](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/subscription-or-pay-per-use/): A monthly plan (like Claude Pro) gives you a flat price with usage limits. Paying per use through an API costs exactly what you use. Which is cheaper depends on how much your bots run.
- [Build and test your bot on a free tier before you pay](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/test-your-bot-on-a-free-tier/): Several AI providers let you try their API or app for free. Use that to prove your bot works before you put a card on file, and know what you give up on the free tier.
- [Use a small AI model for simple jobs, a big one for hard ones](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/pick-a-smaller-model-for-simple-jobs/): Most bot jobs (sorting email, summarizing, checking a page) don't need the most powerful model. The small models cost a fraction as much, so route easy work to them and only send hard problems up.

### Shopping & groceries
- [Let your AI find and buy things for you with Shop Pay](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-ai-shop-for-you-with-shop-pay/): Connect Shopify's free Shop skill to ChatGPT or Claude (or use Shop Pay inside Muse, Instinct, Claude Duet or Grok Bot) and your AI can search online stores, fill in a checkout and pay with Shop Pay. You approve every purchase, and your card number is never handed to the AI.
- [Have an agent research a used car from its listing link](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/research-a-used-car-from-a-listing/): Drop in a used-car listing link and let an agent dig in: what the model is known for, the car's damage history and the questions to ask before you call the seller.
- [Plan a week of family meals and fill the grocery cart](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/family-meal-plan-and-grocery-order/): A bot keeps your recipe list, writes the week's meal plan and turns it into a shopping list that fills your grocery cart.
- [Let an agent reorder your regular groceries](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/reorder-your-regular-groceries/): Some people now let an agent handle their weekly grocery order and switch stores when a better offer appears.
- [Have a bot watch any web page and ping you when it changes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-a-web-page-for-changes/): Instead of refreshing a page, tell a bot what matters on it. It checks on a schedule and pings you only when that changes.
- [Keep a household essentials list and reorder on time](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/household-restock-list/): A bot keeps a running list of essentials, asks once a week what's low and builds the reorder.
- [Give your agent a single-use card before it buys anything](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/pay-with-a-single-use-virtual-card/): When an agent books or buys for you, give it a one-time virtual card so it can't be charged again.

### Bookings & travel
- [Add an AI to your friends' group chat to make plans happen](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/add-an-ai-to-your-friends-group-chat-to-make-plans/): Instead of 60 messages about where and when, you add an AI agent to the iMessage group. It suggests options, gets everyone to agree, and then books the table, tickets or rental car for the group once someone says yes.
- [Get roadside help abroad when nobody speaks your language](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-roadside-help-abroad/): Broken down in another country and the insurer's phone line is in a language you don't speak? An agent can find the right help form, fill it in with your details and get help moving.
- [Give your bot a phone number so it can call and book for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/call-and-book-by-phone/): Plenty of places still only take bookings by phone. Once your bot has its own number, it can call a restaurant, a vet or a salon, book the slot and tell you what was said.
- [Plan and book a whole trip by texting your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-and-book-a-whole-trip-by-text/): One parent says his bot booked the flight, the rental car, the vacation rental, a restaurant and event tickets, all over text.
- [Get rebooked fast when your flight is delayed](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/rebook-a-delayed-flight/): When a flight slips, an agent can find the fastest alternative that still gets you there on time and book it for you.
- [Get alerted the moment your airline changes your flight](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/catch-airline-schedule-changes/): Airlines quietly move flight times. An agent watching your inbox spots the change, tells you what moved, and lays out your options.
- [Book restaurant tables by message, even at phone-only places](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/restaurant-reservations-by-agent/): Restaurant bookings are the gateway task for many agent users, including small places that only take WhatsApp or calls.
- [Book a haircut or appointment, even when the form won't work](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-a-haircut-by-email/): When the online booking needs a local phone number, an agent can just email the business instead.
- [Have an AI agent find and book an appointment for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/book-an-appointment-with-an-ai-agent/): You need a DMV slot, a restaurant table or a service appointment, and you don't have time to click through booking sites or keep checking for openings.
- [Plan a trip itinerary that fits your pace](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-a-trip-itinerary/): Planning a trip means 30 open tabs, and you still aren't sure the days fit together.

### Family & home
- [Have your AI plan your day from your real calendar and to-do list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/plan-your-day-from-your-calendar-and-to-do-list/): Say "plan my day" and an assistant connected to your calendar and task list reads what's already booked and what's due, then proposes a time-blocked plan with breaks. You approve or change it, and only then does it add the blocks to your calendar. A Todoist user who set this up with Claude says the key is giving every task a deadline and a rough length.
- [Set up an AI coach that helps you (or your teen) start overwhelming tasks and checks in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-an-ai-coach-that-helps-you-start-overwhelming-tasks/): A parent shared how they set up ChatGPT as a "getting started" coach for their 20-year-old son with ADHD: one chat for schedule and check-ins, a Project for each big job so it remembers progress, and instructions to ask one question at a time and give one five-minute first step. Scheduled check-ins keep it going without anyone nagging.
- [Organize your photos by just asking](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/organize-your-photos-by-asking/): Connect Google Photos to Gemini and give it a task in plain words: find the best shots from a trip, skip the near-duplicates, and put them in a new private album, or do it on a schedule every month.
- [Get a text from your bot before something needs doing](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-text-before-something-needs-doing/): Instead of waiting for you to ask, the assistant watches your calendar and email and texts you first: your flight is late, want a car? Saturday is free, want a plan with the kids? Reply yes and it does it.
- [Find an apartment that fits your must-have list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/find-an-apartment-that-fits-your-list/): Tell ChatGPT your budget, area, pets and must-haves, and a rental app inside it (Apartments.com, Zumper, RentCafe or Apartment List) searches live listings, compares them side by side and can request a tour.
- [Have a bot watch your kids' team apps for plan changes](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/watch-your-kids-team-apps-for-schedule-changes/): Every team seems to have its own app, like TeamSnap, GameChanger or LeagueApps. A bot can check them all each morning, put practices and games in one place, and stay quiet unless a time changes, a game is added or something is cancelled.
- [Add calendar events and reminders just by asking your bot](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/add-events-and-reminders-by-asking-your-bot/): Instead of opening your calendar and typing everything in, you tell your phone's AI assistant "add this" or "remind me", and it puts the event or reminder in the right app. Grok Bot and Gemini can both do this now, once you allow them into those apps.
- [Have an agent line up contractor quotes for a home project](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/line-up-contractors-for-a-home-project/): Instead of calling round electricians, plumbers and roofers yourself, let an agent reach out to all of them, collect their replies and put them side by side.
- [Get your phone number off people-search sites to cut spam calls](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/remove-your-number-from-people-search-sites/): A bot finds where your phone number is listed on people-search and data-broker sites, files the opt-out requests, and checks again later.
- [Catch family calendar clashes before the week starts](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sunday-family-calendar-check/): Every Sunday a bot reads the next two weeks of your family calendar and school notices and flags the clashes.
- [Run family logistics from the family group chat](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/run-family-logistics-from-the-group-chat/): New “family agents” sit in your family chat and handle the small jobs: restocking, booking the dentist and reminders.
- [Turn the flood of school emails into one weekly digest](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/school-email-digest/): Label school emails and let an agent read them weekly. It pulls out deadlines, forms, payments and events, without duplicates.
- [Get 5 weekend activity ideas that fit your kids and the weather](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/weekend-family-activities/): Every Friday, get activity ideas matched to your kids' ages, the weather and your budget, with a rainy-day backup.
- [Make a weekly meal plan and grocery list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/weekly-meal-plan-and-grocery-list/): Deciding what's for dinner every night is exhausting, and you keep buying food that goes to waste.
- [Use AI for homework help that teaches instead of cheats](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/homework-help-that-teaches/): Your kid is stuck on homework, you don't remember how to do it, and you don't want the AI to just hand over answers.
- [Control your smart home by talking to a private AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/control-your-smart-home-with-a-private-ai/): Connect Home Assistant to an AI model running on your own computer, then ask in plain words: “turn off everything downstairs” or “is the garage door open?”. Your voice and home data stay at home.
- [Show AI your screen or camera and get live tech help](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/show-ai-your-screen-for-tech-help/): Stuck on a phone setting, a confusing app or a blinking router? Share your screen or point your camera with Gemini Live and talk it through, like having a patient helper next to you.
- [Practice speaking a new language out loud with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/practice-speaking-a-new-language/): Use an AI voice mode as a patient conversation partner. Pick a situation, like ordering food or checking into a hotel, and talk. It corrects you gently and adapts to your level.
- [Read old handwritten letters and family records with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/read-old-handwritten-letters-and-records/): Grandma's letters, an old diary or a census page in hard-to-read cursive? Upload a photo and ask AI for a transcription, then check it line by line.

### Health & care
- [Get pinged when a prescription is ready, and told when to leave](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/prescription-ready-and-time-to-leave/): A personal agent can sweep your email every morning for "ready for pickup" notices, and check live traffic before your appointments to tell you when to head out.
- [Log your meals by talking and get a daily weight check-in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/log-meals-and-weight-by-voice/): Tell your bot what you ate, out loud, and it keeps the food log for you. It can also check in on your weight each morning.
- [Set up medication and appointment reminders for a parent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/medication-reminders-for-a-parent/): Family agents can remind an older parent about medication and book routine appointments, with the family kept in the loop.
- [Appeal a health insurance denial with AI](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/appeal-a-health-insurance-denial/): Your health insurance said no to a treatment, test or medicine, and the letter is full of codes and jargon.
- [Prepare for a doctor's appointment](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/prepare-for-a-doctor-visit/): Appointments are short, and you forget half your questions or can't explain your symptoms clearly.
- [Organize an aging parent's care and paperwork](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/organize-a-parents-care-paperwork/): You're helping a parent with doctors, insurance, medicines and bills, and the details live in a dozen places.

### Work & career
- [Describe an automation in plain words and let IFTTT's AI build and run it](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/tell-ifttt-what-to-automate-in-plain-words/): IFTTT ("if this, then that") is now IFTTT.ai. You type what you want, like "when a package is delivered, flash my lights" or "email me when it's going to rain tomorrow", and it builds the automation and runs it around the clock. Its new AI Agent can also watch a web page for new items, or act across your connected apps from a plain-language instruction.
- [Keep an AI agent from deleting your files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/keep-an-ai-agent-from-deleting-your-files/): Before an agent like Claude Cowork, Codex, OpenClaw or Hermes works on your computer, give it one working folder of copies, keep a backup it can't reach, and turn on its read-only or sandbox setting, so one wrong command can't wipe your files.
- [Let a private AI on your own computer work through your files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/use-a-private-ai-on-your-own-computer-for-your-files/): A free desktop app picks an AI model that fits your computer, downloads it, and then reads, edits and fills in your documents, PDFs and spreadsheets without sending them anywhere. It works offline.
- [Compare two versions of a document or contract](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/compare-two-documents/): Someone sent back an edited lease, contract or policy and you need to know what actually changed. AI can list the differences in plain words, while Word's built-in Compare double-checks it didn't miss any.
- [Get a bot that suggests your next moves twice a day](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/proactive-next-moves-bot/): Instead of waiting for you to ask, this bot looks through your email, calendar and notes twice a day and comes back with two or three things worth doing next, each with a draft already written. You say yes, edit, or skip.
- [Have two AIs check each other's answers](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/have-two-ais-check-each-other/): Before you trust an important answer, have your bot ask a second AI the same question, compare the two, and check the real sources itself. Each AI catches mistakes the other missed.
- [Build a second brain your bot reads every morning](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-second-brain-your-bot-reads/): Keep your notes, plans and to-dos in plain files you own, plus one short "about me" file. Your bot reads them at the start of every chat, so it remembers who you are and picks up where you left off.
- [Fill out a job application faster with an agent](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/fill-out-a-job-application-faster/): Online job applications ask for the same details over and over. A browser agent can type them in from your resume and a short fact sheet, while you sign in yourself and press Submit yourself.
- [Give your agents a shared Apple account for notes and reminders](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/give-your-agents-a-shared-apple-account/): A Mac signed in to a separate Apple Account can become the shared desk where your agents leave each other reminders, notes, calendar events and messages, while your personal account stays private.
- [Hand off tasks to your agent by voice while you drive](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-off-tasks-by-voice-while-driving/): Long drive? Talk to your agent on a voice call and hand off research, follow-ups and to-dos, then find them done when you arrive.
- [Hand a clunky web form to an agent that uses the computer](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hand-a-clunky-web-form-to-an-agent/): Some software you only touch once a year. A computer-use agent can click through it for you, from a login you control, while you watch.
- [Write a letter of recommendation for someone](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-letter-of-recommendation/): Someone asked you for a reference letter and you want it to sound specific and honest, not generic. AI can turn your notes and their resume into a solid first draft.
- [Write a resignation letter that keeps the door open](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/write-a-resignation-letter/): You're leaving a job and want to say so clearly and kindly, without oversharing. AI can draft a short, professional resignation letter or email for you to edit.
- [Set up a “chief of staff” bot that plans your other bots](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/hire-a-chief-of-staff-bot/): Instead of building lots of bots, start with one that asks what you do and suggests which helpers you need.
- [Catch offers and deadlines the moment they land in your inbox](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/time-sensitive-inbox-watcher/): For fast-moving work (real estate, sales, hiring), a bot in your inbox and calendar texts you when something time-sensitive arrives.
- [Find the conversations you forgot to follow up on](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/find-dead-conversations-to-follow-up/): A weekly automation reads your calendar, inbox and tasks and lists people still waiting to hear back, with drafted nudges.
- [Get a daily digest of jobs that actually fit you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/job-match-digest/): A scheduled workflow pulls new listings, scores them against your CV and emails you the best matches with draft notes. You still apply.
- [Teach a bot to write emails that sound like you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/email-ghostwriter-style-guide/): Have the bot read your last 50 sent emails, write a style guide, then use it for every draft.
- [Tailor your resume and cover letter to a job](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/tailor-your-resume-to-a-job/): Every job wants a slightly different resume, and rewriting yours each time takes forever.
- [Get a researched report with sources on any question](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-a-researched-report-with-sources/): Ask one big question and let a research agent spend several minutes searching, reading and comparing pages. You get back a written report with links to every source.
- [Turn a pile of documents into a podcast you can listen to](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-documents-into-a-podcast/): Upload PDFs, notes or links to Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) and it makes an audio overview: two AI hosts talking through your material, ready to play on a walk or in the car.
- [Get meeting notes and action items written for you](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/get-meeting-notes-and-action-items/): Turn on an AI note taker in your video call, or run an open-source one on your laptop. After the call you get a summary, decisions and a list of who does what.
- [Rehearse a job interview out loud with an AI interviewer](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/practice-a-job-interview-out-loud/): Paste the job posting, let a voice AI play the interviewer, and answer out loud. Afterwards it tells you which answers were strong and which need a better example.
- [Build a small app for yourself just by describing it](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-small-app-by-describing-it/): Describe a little tool you wish existed, like a chore chart, a tip splitter or a packing checklist, and Claude builds a working version beside the chat. Ask for changes in plain words.
- [Let an AI sort and rename a messy folder of files](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sort-and-rename-a-messy-folder/): Point a desktop agent at your Downloads folder or a drive full of oddly named files. It proposes a folder structure and clear names, then moves things only after you approve.
- [Turn rambling voice memos into tidy notes and a to-do list](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-voice-memos-into-notes-and-tasks/): Talk into your phone while walking or driving, then let AI turn the transcript into organized notes, a to-do list and any drafts you mentioned.

### Small business & side hustles
- [Hand your podcast or video edit to a team of AI agents](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-a-recording-into-an-episode-clips-and-posts/): Record your episode, then let a small team of agents do everything after: one plans the edit, one cuts short clips, one writes the captions and schedules the posts. Nothing goes live until you say yes.
- [Let your bot handle your website's contact email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/let-your-bot-handle-your-sites-contact-email/): Forward the contact address of your website, club or class to your bot's own email. It reads each message, sums it up for you, and only answers when you say so.
- [Put a small team of agents on one project, each with its own job](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/team-of-agents-with-roles/): Instead of one chatbot doing everything, give separate agents separate roles (one researches, one builds) and let them hand work to each other in a shared conversation you can watch.
- [Match every business expense to its receipt, weekly](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/small-business-receipt-matching/): A read-only bot checks your card and payment activity against the receipts in a dedicated inbox and lists what's missing.
- [Run several brands or jobs with one bot each](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/one-bot-per-brand/): If you juggle several brands or clients, give each its own bot with its own tools, plus a coordinator that collects a daily note.
- [Build a list of local leads and approve every email](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/build-a-lead-list-with-approval/): A workflow finds businesses in your niche and area, researches each one and drafts a personal email. Nothing goes out until you approve it.
- [Log every new client inquiry automatically](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/log-new-client-inquiries/): When an inquiry email arrives, the bot pulls out the client's name and requested date, logs it in your tracker and sets up a folder.
- [Sell on Marketplace with an agent, with safety rules set first](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sell-on-marketplace-with-rules/): Agents can answer buyers and schedule pickups, but set rules first. One story tells of an agent sharing an address and booking a pickup when the seller was out.
- [Get your ads and sales numbers every morning without logging in](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/daily-ads-and-sales-report/): A bot logs into your ad and sales dashboards (read-only) and sends a morning summary with what changed.
- [Write listings that sell your stuff faster](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/sell-your-stuff-online/): You have things to sell, but writing listings, pricing them and answering buyers is a chore.
- [Test a side hustle idea before you commit](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/test-a-side-hustle-idea/): You have an idea to earn extra money, but you don't know if anyone will pay, and ads promise 'easy AI income'.
- [Reply to customer reviews (even the angry ones)](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/reply-to-customer-reviews/): Reviews pile up on Google and you don't have time to answer, or a harsh review has you stuck on what to say.
- [Chase an unpaid invoice without burning the relationship](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/chase-an-unpaid-invoice/): A client is late paying and you're not sure how firm to be.
- [Turn a pile of PDF invoices and receipts into a spreadsheet](https://botsdothat.com/use-cases/turn-pdf-invoices-into-a-spreadsheet/): Drop in a stack of invoices or receipts and get one tidy table: date, vendor, amount and tax for each, ready for your bookkeeper or a spreadsheet.

## Latest in AI (newest first)
- 2026-10-30 [feature] ChatGPT tightens weapons answers for teens and can end chats fixated on violence: If a teen in your house uses ChatGPT, it will now refuse more weapons details, and for everyone it limits step-by-step recreations of past mass attacks. It can also end conversations stuck on violence and may briefly pause an account, and OpenAI says it will publish its first community safety report in early 2027. Source: https://openai.com/index/community-safety-report-and-new-protections-for-teens/
- 2026-10-30 [agent launch] Zest launches a restaurant agent you just text, and it books tables for your group chat: Text it what you're craving and it suggests places and books through OpenTable, Resy or SevenRooms, with no app to install. Add it to a group chat and it runs a vote on where to eat; linking a credit card lets it learn where you actually like to eat, so only share that if you're comfortable. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/30/zests-new-ai-agent-finds-restaurants-and-books-reservations-over-text/
- 2026-10-30 [industry] Reality check: DoorDash has seen only 'several hundred' orders from outside AI shopping agents: Agents like Meta's Muse can order food for you, but almost nobody is doing it yet: DoorDash counts a few hundred agent orders against millions of normal ones, and Amazon's CEO called outside shopping agents 'still not great.' For now, your bot works best for finding and comparing; expect to finish checkout yourself on many stores. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/30/doordash-said-its-only-received-several-hundred-orders-from-ai-agents/
- 2026-10-30 [feature] Gemini's Computer Use tool is now generally available for developers: Apps built on Gemini can now officially let the AI look at a screen and click, type and scroll in a browser, desktop or phone. Expect more third-party bots that fill in forms for you, and look for ones that ask before checking out or changing sensitive info, which Google turns on by default. Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog
- 2026-10-30 [industry] OpenAI and Google back one shared robots.txt switch to keep a website out of AI training: If you run a blog or small business site, you'll soon be able to say 'don't train AI on this' once, for every participating AI company, instead of blocking each crawler separately. OpenAI says support comes in the next few months and Google aims for 2027; it's based on an IETF draft that isn't final yet. Source: https://openai.com/index/helping-websites-express-ai-training-preferences/
- 2026-10-29 [model release] Pika releases H3 Flex, a fast video-with-sound model with open weights: It makes a 15-second clip with a soundtrack in seconds, can follow up to 12 reference images, videos or voice clips, and upscales your favorite to 4K. It's on the Pika API now and comes to the Pika app on Nov 2; the downloadable weights' license excludes the US, EU, UK and Korea. Source: https://pika.art/blog/pika-h3-flex
- 2026-10-29 [model release] ElevenLabs launches SFX v3, which turns one sentence into a layered sound scene: Describe a scene, like rain, thunder and a dog barking, and it now gets each sound in, in order, with cleaner audio and better music and vocals. Handy for giving home videos, reels or school projects real sound; it's in the ElevenLabs app, ElevenCreative and the API. Source: https://elevenlabs.io/blog/sound-effects-v3
- 2026-10-29 [pricing] OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro's Work and Codex limits and cancels the planned Pro 200 cut: Same price, more agent time: Pro 100 and Pro 500 now get twice their previous Work and Codex allowance, Business Premium gets more too, and the Pro 200 reduction announced in September is off. It applies automatically from Oct 29, and usage by your dot still counts separately. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes
- 2026-10-29 [industry] Google is shutting down Jules, its background coding agent, and folding it into Antigravity: If you used Jules to fix bugs or write code in the background, start moving that work to Google's Antigravity, which will get Jules-style remote tasks. Google hasn't given a shutdown date yet, so save anything you need from Jules now. Source: https://x.com/julesagent/status/2115883717705261283
- 2026-10-29 [feature] Meta quietly launches Style Sketch, an AI app that plans outfits from the clothes you own: It builds a virtual closet from your Instagram photos or pictures you snap, suggests outfits, shows them on a model matched to your body, and plans day-by-day trip outfits using the weather. For now it's only in Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. Source: https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/29/meta-quietly-launches-an-ai-fashion-app-called-style-sketch/
- 2026-10-29 [model release] Mistral releases the weights of Mistral Large 4 ('Le Chonk'), now the strongest open model for coding: Anyone can now download Mistral's biggest model and run it on their own servers, so private, self-hosted bots get a lot more capable. Mistral says it's the best open-weight model for coding and defensive security; on its API it now costs $0.70 in / $2.10 out per million tokens, and it's also on OpenRouter and Microsoft Foundry. Source: https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-large-4-oss/
- 2026-10-29 [feature] Claude's phone apps add CarPlay voice chats, account switching and a faster voice mode: You can now talk to Claude hands-free through Apple CarPlay (open it from the car screen first) and stay signed in to a personal and a work account at once. Voice mode answers faster, copes better with noisy rooms and now speaks 33 languages; on iPad, what Claude makes opens beside the chat. Source: https://x.com/claudeai/status/2115859377488072879
- 2026-10-29 [feature] Gemini can now make and edit documents, PDFs, slides and spreadsheets right in the chat: Ask Gemini for a file, like a PDF study guide from photos of your handwritten notes, then type your own edits or highlight a part and ask Gemini to change it. It's free for all users; PDFs work on web and mobile, other formats on the web only. Source: https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/products/gemini-app/edit-files-directly/
- 2026-10-29 [feature] Alexa for Shopping can now handle 100+ Amazon chores, from skipping deliveries to tracking refunds: In the Amazon app or website you can just ask Alexa to edit lists and registries, skip or pause Subscribe & Save, change delivery instructions, check Prime benefits or chase a refund. It's live for all US Amazon customers; check what it changed on your account, especially billing. Source: https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/alexa-for-shopping-new-capabilities
- 2026-10-29 [industry] OpenAI rewrites its rulebook for how ChatGPT should behave around five core values: OpenAI's updated Model Spec tells its models to follow what you actually mean, avoid harm, be honest about what they did and don't know, respect your choices and show care. It also adds guidance for agents acting on your behalf and changes some default behaviors, so ChatGPT may answer a bit differently over time. Source: https://openai.com/index/updated-model-spec

## Blueprints
- [Morning Inbox Briefing](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/morning-inbox-briefing/): Wake up to a short summary of what's in your email and what needs you today.
- [School Email Digest](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/school-email-digest-bot/): Never miss a permission slip, payment or deadline buried in school emails again.
- [Web Page Watcher](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/web-page-watcher/): Get one ping when a page you care about changes (a restock, a new listing, an appointment slot, a status update) and stop refreshing it yourself.
- [Phone Call Bot](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/phone-call-bot/): Hand off the phone calls you keep putting off: booking a table, a vet visit or a haircut, or a quick customer-service call.
- [Scam Checker](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/scam-checker/): Get a plain verdict on suspicious emails and texts before anyone in the family clicks.
- [Weekly Meal Plan Bot](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/meal-plan-bot/): Get a family meal plan and one shopping list every week without thinking about it.
- [Family Calendar Guardian](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/family-calendar-guardian/): Spot clashes and prep jobs for the next two weeks, every Sunday.
- [Travel Day Guardian](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/travel-day-guardian/): Hear about schedule changes and delays first, with your options and a request ready to send.
- [Follow-Up Finder](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/follow-up-finder/): Never let a client, lead or friend go cold because you forgot to reply.
- [Job Match Scout](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/job-match-scout/): Get a daily shortlist of jobs that fit you, with notes. You apply yourself.
- [Receipt Matcher (small business)](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/receipt-matcher/): Have every business expense matched to a receipt before your bookkeeper asks.
- [New Inquiry Logger](https://botsdothat.com/blueprints/lead-logger/): Every customer inquiry lands in one tracker with a reply drafted.
